surfaces.part: cave ceiling band with stalactites hanging down

answer.evidence: The object is a flat row of stalactites. A 48px-wide band at rows 0-3 narrows into tapering spikes down to row 14. The silhouette shrinks steadily with no widening-then-narrowing, so there is no ellipse. No front-edge line or eave shadow marks a horizontal surface. The column scan shows only mottled shading on a vertical face. It reads as a flat wall-mounted face-on drawing, so front_elevation fits a wall_mounted kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin, sparse row of hanging stalactites, so I judged density by eye. It has 9 visible tones per tile, matching the hedge reference (9) but below the well (20) and the cheese stall (17). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. Shading shows about 4 stone steps (light top, mid, dark, shadow tips) with some speckle, but each spike is a simple triangular form with little per-stone shading or grain, so it looks thinner and flatter than the well, stall and hedge. Dark edge pixels are 37% neutral, so the outline is mixed. It is partly tinted, but some edge pixels lean grey and stay close to the uniform sticker look. Next to the richer references, an artist would likely see it as a little thin and under-shaded.

The column scans show only alternating light and mid-tone shading stripes, with no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse, and no visible contents. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a row of hanging stalactites with a lighter rock band along the top. It carries 9 visible tones per tile, equal to prop-hedge (9) and below prop-well-roofed (20) and prop-stall-cheese (17).
